exchanges: Good afternoon. I've just come in from the community garden and I'm making a pot of tea.
Good afternoon. That sounds like a nice way to wind down. How was the garden today?
Busy. We're clearing the bean rows before the frost. Arjun, our coordinator, had everyone working in pairs.
Working in pairs makes the big jobs go faster.
It does. He brought his dog along, a scruffy little thing called Pepper, who dug up half the carrots.
That sounds like a dog who wanted to help in his own way.
Exactly. I bought a new wheelbarrow last week, so at least I could haul the weeds away easily.
A good one saves a lot of strain on the back.
My son Kwame phoned while I was out there. He's been on night shifts all month.
Night shifts are hard. What does he do?
He's a paramedic, has been for about twelve years now. I worry, but he loves it.
It is natural to worry, and it is good that he finds meaning in the work.
My daughter's husband Daniel is the opposite, he's an electrician and home every evening by five.
Two very different schedules in one family.
Yes, and they argue about it at Christmas, which is funny to watch.
Family debates can be the best entertainment.
My neighbour Ingrid is off to Tuscany next month with her book club.
A book club trip sounds wonderful.
I'm a little jealous. The furthest I've been this year is the garden centre.
The garden centre has its own charms.
I'm Ghanaian by heritage, and my mother grew yams and okra in our backyard. That's where I learned to garden.
It is lovely that the habit came down from her.
Speaking of my mother, I've been practising the cello again, the one she bought me when I was ten.
Coming back to an instrument after a long time can be very rewarding.
My fingers are stiff but it's coming back slowly.
Little by little is the way.
I've also started aqua fit at the community pool. It's every Monday morning at eight.
Water exercise is gentle on the joints. How do you like it?
I enjoy it more than I expected. The instructor plays Motown.
Music always makes a workout easier.
My grandson Yusuf came round for dinner on Sunday. He's grown so tall.
Grandchildren seem to grow so fast.
He told us he's been accepted to McGill for the autumn. We were all so proud.
That is a wonderful achievement. Congratulations to him.
Thank you. I'll miss him when he moves to Montreal.
It is not too far for visits.
Oh, I need to correct something. Ingrid isn't going to Tuscany after all, she said Sicily. I mixed it up with her last trip.
Thanks for the correction. That should be lovely at that time of year.
Gerald and I are having our fortieth anniversary party in the spring. We've booked the Boathouse by the river.
Forty years is something to celebrate.
We had our wedding reception near there, so it felt right.
That gives it a nice connection to the start.
I still need to sort out the guest list. That will take weeks.
Starting early is wise.
The kettle's whistling again, I'll have a second cup.
Enjoy it.
My friend Lucia is coming over tomorrow.
That sounds nice. Do you have plans?
We'll probably just talk for hours, as usual.
The best kind of visit.
She wants to take me to her favourite café afterwards, a place called Moonbeam on Queen Street.
That sounds like a nice outing. Have you been there before?
Never. She says their scones are the best in the city.
Then you will have to try one.
Remind me, what does my son-in-law do for work?

earlier_question.right_reply: Daniel, your son-in-law, is an electrician.
earlier_question.wrong_reply: Daniel, your son-in-law, is a paramedic.

questions.message: Which university did Yusuf get into?
Which day is my water exercise class?
What venue did we choose for the forty-year celebration?
Where does Lucia like to go for coffee?
I think I'll do the crossword before bed tonight.
Does Ingrid have a pet? What's its name?
Is Gerald planning any trips this year?
Sorry, Daniel's job, what was it again?
